answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when a result is proven fraudulent through a challenge window. Reputation attaches to the locked stake and completed work, not merely to an address, so minting a thousand identities does not create a thousand trusted workers. The attacker must acquire and immobilize real capital, risk losing it, and wait for reputation to accrue. A quartz kernel may whisper through the interface, but it cannot make those costs disappear.
